note: Logit-authored Logstash filter documentation. Single source of truth for per-plugin description, options, and example blocks. Factual fields (name/required/type/default) mirror the public plugin interface; all prose and example blocks are written in-house.

age.description: Calculates how old each event is by subtracting the event `@timestamp` from the current time. The resulting age (in seconds) is written to a field you can use for conditional routing, stale-event dropping, or TTL-style processing.

options.name: target
options.description: Field where the calculated age value (in seconds) is written.

aggregate.description: Groups information across events that share a common task identifier so you can produce correlated outputs (such as transaction durations, per-session summaries, or paired request/response records). State is held in memory per pipeline worker, which means you should run aggregating pipelines on a single worker.

options.name: code
options.description: Ruby code executed on each matching event; the shared state is available as `map` and the current event as `event`.

options.name: task_id
options.description: Sprintf expression that produces the shared task key used to correlate related events (for example `%{transaction_id}`).

options.name: aggregate_maps_path
options.description: File path used to persist aggregate state across pipeline restarts.

options.name: end_of_task
options.description: When true, deletes the map entry for the task after the code block runs (use this on the event that ends the task).

options.name: inactivity_timeout
options.description: Seconds without a new event before a task is flushed (must be lower than `timeout`).

options.name: map_action
options.description: Controls whether the filter creates a new map entry, updates an existing one, or both (`create`, `update`, or `create_or_update`).

options.name: push_map_as_event_on_timeout
options.description: Emit the aggregated state as a new event when the task times out.

options.name: push_previous_map_as_event
options.description: Emit the previous task's aggregated state when a new task id is seen (requires events to arrive in order).

options.name: timeout
options.description: Seconds to retain an idle task before it is considered complete and optionally emitted.

options.name: timeout_code
options.description: Ruby code run against the new event produced by a timeout flush.

options.name: timeout_tags
options.description: Tags added to events produced by timeout flushes to help downstream routing.

options.name: timeout_task_id_field
options.description: Field on the flushed event that stores the originating task id.

options.name: timeout_timestamp_field
options.description: Timestamp field on the flushed event; uses the last seen event time when set.

options.name: map_count_warning_threshold
options.description: Logs a warning when the number of in-memory aggregate maps exceeds this threshold.

alter.description: Applies field-level alterations that do not fit the `mutate` filter: conditional replacement, fallback values, and coalesce operations across several fields.

options.name: coalesce
options.description: Takes the first non-null value from a list of fields and writes it to a destination field.

options.name: condrewrite
options.description: Rewrites a field value only when it matches a supplied condition.

options.name: condrewriteother
options.description: Conditionally rewrites a different field based on the source field's value.

bytes.description: Parses storage-size strings such as `123 MB` or `5.6gb` and converts them into numeric byte values. Useful when upstream systems emit human-readable sizes that you need to query, chart, or alert on numerically.

options.name: target
options.description: Field where the numeric byte value will be written.

options.name: source
options.description: Field that contains the human-readable size string.

options.name: conversion_method
options.description: Conversion base used when interpreting the size (`binary` for 1024-based units or `decimal` for 1000-based units).

cidr.description: Matches IP addresses against one or more CIDR ranges and lets you take action on matches (for example tag internal traffic, drop known-bad ranges, or route events by network).

options.name: address
options.description: List of IP addresses to check against the configured networks.

options.name: address_field
options.description: Field whose value is used as the IP to check (alternative to `address`).

options.name: network
options.description: List of CIDR blocks to match against (for example `10.0.0.0/8`).

options.name: network_path
options.description: Path to a file containing one CIDR block per line, reloaded at the configured interval.

options.name: refresh_interval
options.description: Seconds between reloads when `network_path` is used.

options.name: separator
options.description: Character used to split multiple CIDR values when loading from a file.

cipher.description: Encrypts or decrypts field values using OpenSSL ciphers. Useful for masking sensitive fields before indexing or for decrypting payloads produced by upstream systems.

options.name: algorithm
options.description: OpenSSL cipher name, such as `aes-256-cbc`.

options.name: mode
options.description: Operation mode; set to `encrypt` to encrypt values or `decrypt` to decrypt them.

options.name: base64
options.description: When true, inputs are treated as (and outputs produced as) base64 strings.

options.name: cipher_padding
options.description: Disable PKCS padding by setting to `0` when the upstream cipher was run without padding.

options.name: iv_random_length
options.description: Length in bytes of a per-event random initialisation vector.

options.name: key
options.description: Cipher key used for the operation; supply through a Logit secret rather than hard-coding.

options.name: key_pad
options.description: Character used to pad a short key up to `key_size`.

options.name: key_size
options.description: Key size in bytes (must match the chosen algorithm).

options.name: max_cipher_reuse
options.description: Maximum number of events that can reuse the same cipher instance before it is recycled.

options.name: source
options.description: Field containing the value to encrypt or decrypt.

options.name: target
options.description: Field to write the transformed value into (defaults to the source field).

clone.description: Duplicates the current event and tags each clone so downstream conditionals can route copies through different processing branches.

options.name: clones
options.description: List of tag values; one clone is created per entry and tagged with the matching value.

options.name: ecs_compatibility
options.description: Controls ECS field compatibility behaviour (`disabled`, `v1`, or `v8`).

csv.description: Parses comma-separated values from a field into named fields, with optional type conversion and header detection.

options.name: autodetect_column_names
options.description: When true, use the first matching event as the header row.

options.name: autogenerate_column_names
options.description: When true, generate column names automatically (`column1`, `column2`, ...).

options.name: columns
options.description: Ordered list of column names matching the CSV layout.

options.name: convert
options.description: Per-column type conversion map (for example `{ "count" => "integer" }`).

options.name: ecs_compatibility
options.description: Controls ECS field compatibility behaviour (`disabled`, `v1`, or `v8`).

options.name: quote_char
options.description: Character used to quote values that contain the separator.

options.name: separator
options.description: Character used as the field separator.

options.name: skip_empty_columns
options.description: Do not create fields for empty columns.

options.name: skip_empty_rows
options.description: Drop events where every column is empty.

options.name: skip_header
options.description: Skip the first matching event when it is a header row.

options.name: source
options.description: Field containing the CSV line to parse.

options.name: target
options.description: Parent field to nest parsed columns under (omit to write to the event root).

date.description: Parses date/time strings from a field and, by default, uses the parsed value as the event's `@timestamp`. This is the standard way to make log timestamps accurate in OpenSearch once an event reaches Logstash.

options.name: locale
options.description: Locale used when parsing month or day names (for example `en`).

options.name: match
options.description: Array containing the source field name followed by one or more date format patterns to try.

options.name: precision
options.description: Number of digits to use for sub-second precision.

options.name: tag_on_failure
options.description: Tags applied to events whose date could not be parsed (defaults to `_dateparsefailure`).

options.name: target
options.description: Target field for the parsed timestamp (defaults to `@timestamp`).

options.name: timezone
options.description: Timezone to use when the source string has no offset (for example `Europe/London`).

de_dot.description: Rewrites field names that contain `.` characters so they play nicely with OpenSearch. By default each dot is replaced with an underscore, producing a flat field name. With `nested => true` the dots are turned into sub-field boundaries instead, producing nested objects.

options.name: fields
options.description: Explicit list of field references to de-dot (for example `["process.name", "[foo][bar.suffix]"]`). If omitted, every top-level field on the event is checked.

options.name: nested
options.description: When true, convert each dotted name into a nested sub-field instead of flattening with `separator` (the separator is forced to `][` internally, so setting both `nested => true` and `separator` at the same time is not useful).

options.name: recursive
options.description: When true, descend into hash-valued fields and de-dot nested keys as well. Expensive; only enable when you know the event can contain dotted keys inside nested objects.

options.name: separator
options.description: Character used to replace each `.` in a field name when `nested` is false. Cannot itself contain a `.`.

dissect.description: Fast, allocation-friendly alternative to `grok` for parsing logs that use fixed delimiters. Use `dissect` for predictable formats and fall back to `grok` only when you need regex flexibility.

options.name: convert_datatype
options.description: Per-field type conversion applied after extraction (for example `{ "status" => "int" }`).

options.name: mapping
options.description: Map of source field to dissect pattern (for example `{ "message" => "%{ts} %{+ts} %{level} %{msg}" }`).

options.name: tag_on_failure
options.description: Tags applied when the dissect pattern does not match.

drop.description: Drops events from the pipeline. Combine it with an enclosing `if` block to discard noisy logs (health checks, known test traffic, deprecated levels) before they are indexed.

options.name: percentage
options.description: Drop only this percentage of matching events (0 to 100); useful for sampling.

elapsed.description: Pairs start and end events that share a common key and writes the elapsed time between them. Useful for measuring per-request latency when the application emits two log lines rather than one.

options.name: end_tag
options.description: Tag that identifies the end event.

options.name: start_tag
options.description: Tag that identifies the start event.

options.name: unique_id_field
options.description: Field shared by the start and end events that correlates the two.

options.name: new_event_on_match
options.description: Emit a new dedicated event for the match instead of annotating the end event.

options.name: timeout
options.description: Seconds to wait for the end event before giving up on the pair.

options.name: keep_start_event
options.description: Keep the start event in the pipeline rather than discarding it once the pair is matched.

environment.description: Reads environment variables at pipeline start and writes their values into the event, typically into `@metadata` for use by downstream filters or outputs.

options.name: add_metadata_from_env
options.description: Map of environment variable name to destination `@metadata` field path.

extractnumbers.description: Scans a text field and extracts every numeric value it can find, writing the results into structured numeric fields for downstream aggregation or alerting.

options.name: source
options.description: Field whose text content will be scanned for numeric values.

fingerprint.description: Generates a stable hash from one or more fields so you can deduplicate events, build reproducible document IDs, or pseudonymise values before indexing.

options.name: method
options.description: Hashing method, for example `SHA1`, `SHA256`, `MURMUR3`, or `UUID`.

options.name: base64encode
options.description: Output the fingerprint as a base64 string rather than hex.

options.name: concatenate_sources
options.description: Combine the values of all source fields before hashing.

options.name: concatenate_all_fields
options.description: Concatenate every field on the event (use with care; order sensitive).

options.name: ecs_compatibility
options.description: Controls ECS field compatibility behaviour (`disabled`, `v1`, or `v8`).

options.name: key
options.description: Optional secret used for keyed hashes such as HMAC-SHA256.

options.name: source
options.description: Field or list of fields to fingerprint.

options.name: target
options.description: Field to receive the generated fingerprint.

geoip.description: Enriches events with location and network metadata for a given IP address. The plugin uses a bundled MaxMind GeoLite2 database so it works without any outbound network calls.

options.name: source
options.description: Field containing the IP address or hostname to look up.

options.name: cache_size
options.description: Number of recent lookups to keep in memory.

options.name: database
options.description: Path to a custom MaxMind database file (mutually exclusive with `default_database_type`).

options.name: default_database_type
options.description: Built-in database to use (`City` or `ASN`).

options.name: ecs_compatibility
options.description: Controls ECS field compatibility behaviour (`disabled`, `v1`, or `v8`).

options.name: fields
options.description: Subset of lookup fields to keep (for example `country_name`, `city_name`, `location`).

options.name: tag_on_failure
options.description: Tags applied when the lookup produces no result.

options.name: target
options.description: Parent field to nest the enrichment output under (defaults to `geoip`).

grok.description: Parses unstructured text using named regex patterns. It is the default tool for converting single-line log messages into structured fields when the format does not fit a simpler alternative such as `dissect`, `csv`, or `kv`.

options.name: break_on_match
options.description: When true, stop trying additional patterns after the first success.

options.name: ecs_compatibility
options.description: Controls ECS field compatibility behaviour (`disabled`, `v1`, or `v8`).

options.name: keep_empty_captures
options.description: Keep captures that matched but produced an empty value.

options.name: match
options.description: Map of source field name to one or more grok patterns; the first match wins.

options.name: named_captures_only
options.description: Only store named captures on the event; discard unnamed groups.

options.name: overwrite
options.description: List of field names that grok is allowed to overwrite on match.

options.name: pattern_definitions
options.description: Inline custom pattern definitions available to this filter instance.

options.name: patterns_dir
options.description: Directories containing additional grok pattern files.

options.name: patterns_files_glob
options.description: Glob used to select pattern files from `patterns_dir`.

options.name: tag_on_failure
options.description: Tags added when no pattern matches.

options.name: tag_on_timeout
options.description: Tags added when pattern evaluation exceeds `timeout_millis`.

options.name: timeout_millis
options.description: Maximum milliseconds spent evaluating a single event's patterns.

options.name: timeout_scope
options.description: Whether the timeout applies per pattern (`pattern`) or across the whole event (`event`).

i18n.description: Normalises non-ASCII text by transliterating accented characters into their closest ASCII equivalents. Useful when downstream systems expect a restricted character set.

options.name: transliterate
options.description: List of field names whose values should be transliterated.

java_uuid.description: Generates a random UUID for each event using the Java implementation. Use this rather than the Ruby `uuid` filter when you want the built-in, core Logstash version.

options.name: target
options.description: Field to receive the generated UUID.

options.name: overwrite
options.description: When true, replace any existing value in the target field.

json.description: Parses a JSON-encoded string stored in a field and promotes its keys into structured event fields. This is the standard way to unpack events that arrive as a single JSON blob inside `message`.

options.name: source
options.description: Field containing the JSON string to parse.

options.name: ecs_compatibility
options.description: Controls ECS field compatibility behaviour (`disabled`, `v1`, or `v8`).

options.name: skip_on_invalid_json
options.description: When true, invalid JSON does not add a parse-failure tag.

options.name: tag_on_failure
options.description: Tags applied when the source is not valid JSON.

options.name: target
options.description: Parent field to nest the parsed keys under (omit to write to the event root).

json_encode.description: Serialises the value of a field into a JSON string. Useful when a downstream consumer expects a flattened JSON payload inside a single field.

options.name: source
options.description: Field whose value will be serialised.

options.name: target
options.description: Field to receive the resulting JSON string (defaults to the source field).

kv.description: Parses key/value pairs inside a text field into structured fields. Works well for URL query strings, structured syslog suffixes, and simple application logs.

options.name: allow_duplicate_values
options.description: Keep duplicate values instead of deduplicating them into an array.

options.name: allow_empty_values
options.description: Keep keys whose value is an empty string.

options.name: default_keys
options.description: Keys to add with default values when missing from the input.

options.name: ecs_compatibility
options.description: Controls ECS field compatibility behaviour (`disabled`, `v1`, or `v8`).

options.name: exclude_keys
options.description: Drop keys listed here.

options.name: field_split
options.description: String that separates pairs from each other (for example `" "` or `"&"`).

options.name: field_split_pattern
options.description: Regex alternative to `field_split` for more complex separators.

options.name: include_brackets
options.description: Treat bracket characters as part of values (useful for `[` and `]`).

options.name: include_keys
options.description: Only keep keys listed here.

options.name: prefix
options.description: Prefix added to every extracted key name.

options.name: recursive
options.description: Recursively parse values that themselves look like key/value strings.

options.name: remove_char_key
options.description: Characters to remove entirely from every key.

options.name: remove_char_value
options.description: Characters to remove entirely from every value.

options.name: source
options.description: Field containing the key/value text.

options.name: target
options.description: Parent field to nest parsed pairs under.

options.name: tag_on_failure
options.description: Tags applied when parsing produces no fields.

options.name: tag_on_timeout
options.description: Tags applied when parsing exceeds `timeout_millis`.

options.name: timeout_millis
options.description: Maximum time in milliseconds to spend parsing a single event.

options.name: transform_key
options.description: Transform every key (`lowercase`, `uppercase`, or `capitalize`).

options.name: transform_value
options.description: Transform every value (`lowercase`, `uppercase`, or `capitalize`).

options.name: trim_key
options.description: Characters to strip from the beginning and end of each key.

options.name: trim_value
options.description: Characters to strip from the beginning and end of each value.

options.name: value_split
options.description: String that separates a key from its value (for example `"="`).

options.name: value_split_pattern
options.description: Regex alternative to `value_split`.

options.name: whitespace
options.description: Whitespace handling mode (`lenient` or `strict`).

math.description: Applies basic arithmetic operations to numeric fields. Use it to compute derived metrics (for example converting milliseconds to seconds) directly inside the pipeline. This plugin is not part of the default Logstash distribution; it is pre-installed on Logit stacks.

metricize.description: Splits a complex event that contains several metrics into one smaller event per metric. Useful when downstream tooling indexes one metric per document.

options.name: metrics
options.description: List of field names in the source event that each represent a metric.

options.name: drop_original_event
options.description: Drop the original combined event after emitting per-metric events.

options.name: metric_field_name
options.description: Field on each output event that stores the metric name.

options.name: value_field_name
options.description: Field on each output event that stores the metric value.

metrics.description: Aggregates metrics (meters, timers, and percentiles) over a rolling window of events and emits the summary as its own event. Useful for producing rate/latency metrics from raw log streams.

options.name: clear_interval
options.description: Seconds after which the internal state is cleared (use to reset rolling windows).

options.name: flush_interval
options.description: Seconds between summary emissions.

options.name: ignore_older_than
options.description: Ignore events older than this many seconds relative to `@timestamp`.

options.name: meter
options.description: List of meter names; one counter per meter is maintained.

options.name: percentiles
options.description: Percentiles to report on timers (for example `[50, 95, 99]`).

options.name: rates
options.description: Rates to report, in minutes (for example `[1, 5, 15]`).

options.name: timer
options.description: Map of timer name to source field path; used for percentile and rate calculations.

mutate.description: General-purpose field editor for Logstash. Use it to rename, convert, replace, remove, copy, split, merge, or case-normalise fields. It is typically the last step before output, where you shape events to match the target schema.

options.name: convert
options.description: Convert field types, for example `{ "count" => "integer", "ratio" => "float" }`.

options.name: copy
options.description: Copy fields; `{ "src" => "dst" }` copies `src` to `dst` without removing `src`.

options.name: gsub
options.description: Regex-based substitution on field values (triples of `field`, `pattern`, `replacement`).

options.name: join
options.description: Join an array field into a single string using a separator.

options.name: lowercase
options.description: Lowercase the listed field values.

options.name: merge
options.description: Merge two fields together (array into array, hash into hash).

options.name: coerce
options.description: Supply a default value when a configured field is missing.

options.name: rename
options.description: Rename fields; accepts either a hash `{ "source" => "destination" }` or an array.

options.name: replace
options.description: Replace a field's value; supports `%{...}` interpolation.

options.name: split
options.description: Split a string field into an array using a delimiter.

options.name: strip
options.description: Strip leading and trailing whitespace from listed fields.

options.name: update
options.description: Update a field only when it already exists.

options.name: uppercase
options.description: Uppercase the listed field values.

options.name: capitalize
options.description: Capitalize the listed field values.

options.name: tag_on_failure
options.description: Tags applied when a mutate action fails.

prune.description: Removes fields from an event to keep only what downstream systems need. You can whitelist fields and values (keep matches) or blacklist them (drop matches), including pattern-based rules.

options.name: blacklist_names
options.description: Regex patterns; field names that match are removed.

options.name: blacklist_values
options.description: Per-field regex values; fields whose value matches are removed.

options.name: interpolate
options.description: Interpolate `%{...}` expressions in values before matching.

options.name: whitelist_names
options.description: Regex patterns; only field names that match are kept.

options.name: whitelist_values
options.description: Per-field regex values; fields whose value matches are kept.

range.description: Checks numeric values or string lengths against bounds and applies actions when an event is inside or outside the expected range.

options.name: negate
options.description: Invert the match so actions fire when the value is outside the range.

options.name: ranges
options.description: Array of range rules; each rule is `[ field, min, max, action ]`.

ruby.description: Executes inline Ruby code against each event. Use it only when built-in filters cannot express the transformation. On Logit.io, the `ruby` filter is gated and requires prior approval from Logit Support before it can run on production pipelines.

options.name: code
options.description: Inline Ruby code to execute; the current event is available as `event`.

options.name: init
options.description: Ruby code executed once when the pipeline starts.

options.name: path
options.description: Path to an external Ruby script; use instead of `code` for long snippets.

options.name: script_params
options.description: Parameters passed into the external script's `register` method.

options.name: tag_on_exception
options.description: Tag added to the event when the Ruby code raises.

options.name: tag_with_exception_message
options.description: Append the exception message as a tag for quick triage.

sleep.description: Pauses the pipeline for a configured interval. Primarily used for throttling or testing; production pipelines should rarely need this.

options.name: every
options.description: Only sleep once every N events.

options.name: replay
options.description: When true, scale the sleep according to each event's timestamp (useful for replay scenarios).

options.name: time
options.description: Seconds to sleep per matching event.

split.description: Takes a single event with an array-valued field and produces one output event per array element, copying all other fields onto each child event.

options.name: field
options.description: Field that holds the array to split over.

options.name: target
options.description: Field on each child event where the individual element is written (defaults to the source field).

options.name: terminator
options.description: String terminator used to split a string field into an array before splitting.

syslog_pri.description: Parses the `PRI` numeric header of a syslog message into its facility and severity components, producing labelled fields you can alert on.

options.name: ecs_compatibility
options.description: Controls ECS field compatibility behaviour (`disabled`, `v1`, or `v8`).

options.name: facility_labels
options.description: Custom facility label list to override the defaults.

options.name: severity_labels
options.description: Custom severity label list to override the defaults.

options.name: syslog_pri_field_name
options.description: Field that contains the numeric PRI value.

options.name: use_labels
options.description: When true, emit human-readable facility and severity labels in addition to numeric fields.

threats_classifier.description: Enriches security log events with metadata about attacker intent. This is a third-party community plugin; review the upstream project before relying on its classifications in production.

throttle.description: Rate-limits events that share a key inside a rolling time window. Combine it with `drop` or a tag to mute floods of repetitive events without losing visibility entirely.

options.name: key
options.description: Sprintf expression that produces the throttle key (events sharing a key count together).

options.name: after_count
options.description: Tag events only after the count exceeds this threshold.

options.name: before_count
options.description: Tag events only before the count reaches this threshold.

options.name: max_age
options.description: Maximum age of a counter before it is discarded.

options.name: max_counters
options.description: Cap on the number of distinct counters kept in memory.

options.name: period
options.description: Length of the rolling window, in seconds.

tld.description: Parses a URL or hostname and writes the top-level domain, registered domain, and subdomain components into structured fields.

options.name: source
options.description: Field containing the URL or hostname to parse.

options.name: target
options.description: Parent field to nest the parsed components under (defaults to `tld`).

translate.description: Looks up values in a dictionary and writes the mapped result to a destination field. Supports inline dictionaries, external YAML/JSON/CSV files, and optional regex-style matching.

options.name: source
options.description: Field whose value is used as the lookup key.

options.name: destination
options.description: Deprecated alias for `target`; prefer `target`.

options.name: dictionary
options.description: Inline key/value dictionary used for the lookup.

options.name: dictionary_path
options.description: Path to an external YAML, JSON, or CSV file containing the dictionary.

options.name: ecs_compatibility
options.description: Controls ECS field compatibility behaviour (`disabled`, `v1`, or `v8`).

options.name: exact
options.description: When true, use exact matching (default); set false for substring replacement.

options.name: fallback
options.description: Value to use when the lookup misses.

options.name: field
options.description: Deprecated alias for `source`; prefer `source`.

options.name: iterate_on
options.description: Iterate the lookup over an array-valued source field.

options.name: override
options.description: Overwrite the target field if it already has a value.

options.name: refresh_interval
options.description: Seconds between reloads of `dictionary_path`.

options.name: regex
options.description: When true, treat dictionary keys as regex patterns.

options.name: refresh_behaviour
options.description: Reload strategy when a dictionary file is updated (`merge` or `replace`).

options.name: target
options.description: Field that receives the mapped value.

options.name: yaml_dictionary_code_point_limit
options.description: YAML parse safety limit for dictionary files.

options.name: yaml_load_strategy
options.description: YAML loader strategy; `safe` is recommended.

truncate.description: Limits the size of one or more fields so large payloads do not bloat stored documents or exceed index field-size limits.

options.name: length_bytes
options.description: Maximum length, in bytes, to keep per field.

options.name: fields
options.description: List of field names to truncate.

urldecode.description: Decodes URL-encoded (percent-encoded) values so escaped characters become readable text. Useful when upstream systems log encoded URLs or form data.

options.name: all_fields
options.description: When true, decode every string field in the event.

options.name: charset
options.description: Character set used when interpreting decoded bytes (for example `UTF-8`).

options.name: field
options.description: Field to decode.

options.name: tag_on_failure
options.description: Tags applied when decoding fails.

useragent.description: Parses user-agent strings into structured fields such as browser, operating system, and device. The plugin uses a bundled regex database so it works without any outbound network calls.

options.name: source
options.description: Field that contains the user-agent string.

options.name: ecs_compatibility
options.description: Controls ECS field compatibility behaviour (`disabled`, `v1`, or `v8`).

options.name: lru_cache_size
options.description: In-memory cache size used to speed up repeated lookups.

options.name: prefix
options.description: Prefix added to each generated field name.

options.name: regexes
options.description: Path to a custom regex YAML file (use the default when possible).

options.name: target
options.description: Parent field to nest parsed components under (defaults to the event root).

uuid.description: Generates a random UUID string for each event. Use it to give every document a stable, unique identifier you can reference from alerts, dashboards, or dedupe jobs.

options.name: target
options.description: Field to receive the generated UUID.

options.name: overwrite
options.description: When true, replace any existing value in the target field.

wurfl_device_detection.description: Enriches events with device-intelligence fields (brand, model, OS, form factor) from the WURFL database. This is a third-party plugin and requires a WURFL data file and license; review the upstream project before relying on it in production.

xml.description: Parses XML content from a field into structured event fields. Supports full tree-to-hash conversion, optional XPath extraction, and namespace handling.

options.name: source
options.description: Field that contains the XML document to parse.

options.name: force_array
options.description: When true, single-element XPath results are stored as single-item arrays for consistency.

options.name: force_content
options.description: When true, text content and attributes are always parsed into hash values.

options.name: namespaces
options.description: Map of namespace prefix to URI for namespace-aware XPath expressions.

options.name: parse_options
options.description: Parser flags for relaxed or strict handling (for example `strict`).

options.name: remove_namespaces
options.description: Strip XML namespaces from parsed element names.

options.name: store_xml
options.description: When true, store the parsed XML tree under `target`.

options.name: suppress_empty
options.description: When true, empty elements are omitted from the output.

options.name: target
options.description: Parent field to nest the parsed XML hash under.

options.name: xpath
options.description: Map of XPath expression to target field for selective extraction.
